subject: System Design
title: Hot Spots and Skew
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Hot Spots and Skew.

hook.text: A celebrity tweets and the partition holding their data receives 1,000x more traffic than others.

buildup.text: Hot spots occur when one partition receives disproportionate traffic due to skewed access patterns.

discovery.text: Adding a random suffix to hot keys spreads load across partitions: userID becomes userID_1, userID_2, etc.

twist.text: The suffix trick works but complicates reads: you must query all suffixed keys and merge the results.

climax.text: Perfectly even distribution is impossible in practice. The goal is to minimize skew, not eliminate it.

punchline.text: Hot spots overload one partition — spread the keys.

quiz.question: What causes hot spots in partitioned systems?
options: Skewed access patterns where one key gets disproportionate traffic
